body:
Hi there :)
To start off, I'm not entirely sure if this is truly a bug or intended behaviour. I found myself surprised by this, though, so I think it warrants at least some mention in the docs :)

### Detailed description

In [our CI](https://github.com/iiasa/ixmp/blob/main/ixmp/testing/__init__.py#L220), we have recently found the need to parametrize a `backend` fixture with two values: `ixmp4` and `jdbc`. To do so, I've found [a recommendation](https://pytest-with-eric.com/introduction/pytest-generate-tests/) to use `pytest_generate_tests()` [like this](https://github.com/iiasa/ixmp/blob/main/ixmp/testing/__init__.py#L166-L174).
`backend` is 'module'-scoped and in turn used by another fixture, `mp`, also of 'module' scope. 
Yesterday, I discovered that when `mp` is used inside a test class (just for grouping some tests) and outside of the class in the same module (which I think of as a file), then `mp` is created once for the class, torn down, and created again for the use outside the class. 

I think this is where we should move to 

### Minimal working example

conftest.py
```python
import pytest


def pytest_generate_tests(metafunc: pytest.Metafunc) -> None:
    if "one_or_two" in metafunc.fixturenames:
        metafunc.parametrize("one_or_two", [1, 2], indirect=True)


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def one_or_two(request: pytest.FixtureRequest):
    print(request.param)


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def foo(one_or_two):
    print("foo")
```

test.py
```python
class TestFoo:
    def test_foo(self, foo):
        pass


def test_foo(foo):
    pass
```

When I run `pytest test.py`, all four tests (parametrization!) run fine, and when I run `pytest test.py --setup-plan`, I see this:

```
collected 4 items                                                                                                            

test.py 
    SETUP    M one_or_two[1]
    SETUP    M foo (fixtures used: one_or_two)
        test.py::TestFoo::test_foo[1] (fixtures used: foo, one_or_two, request)
        test.py::test_foo[1] (fixtures used: foo, one_or_two, request)
    TEARDOWN M foo
    TEARDOWN M one_or_two[1]
    SETUP    M one_or_two[2]
    SETUP    M foo (fixtures used: one_or_two)
        test.py::TestFoo::test_foo[2] (fixtures used: foo, one_or_two, request)
        test.py::test_foo[2] (fixtures used: foo, one_or_two, request)
    TEARDOWN M foo
    TEARDOWN M one_or_two[2]
```

### Expectations

I noticed this because in our CI, `mp` sets up a DB connection and inserts some data, then yields the connection (more or less). For a recently added test case, all setup data were present twice in the connection, which surprised me. I would have expected `mp` to be setup only once for the whole module since the parametrization happens for a fixture that's also 'module'-scoped. 
But maybe this is as expected because each function gets its own `request` context?

### Technical details

I'm using Ubuntu 24.04 and used `uv` to create a fresh virtual environment with Python 3.12 to produce this MWE:

```
~/t/debug-pytest> uv pip list
Package   Version
--------- -------
iniconfig 2.1.0
packaging 25.0
pluggy    1.6.0
pygments  2.19.2
pytest    8.4.2
```

Please let me know if there's anything else you need :)


### A curious note

When I remove `indirect=True` from the MWE above, all tests fail with an error message like

```
ERROR test.py::test_foo[2] - Failed: ScopeMismatch: You tried to access the function scoped fixture one_or_two with a module scoped request object. Re...
```

Which makes it sound like the scope of `one_or_two` is changed implicitly by the parametrization.
